name: append

arguments.name: str
arguments.description: The string to be appended to the current buffer sequence

use: Appends the characters of the specified String to the end of the existing character sequence in-place. If the parameter str is null, the four characters "null" are appended without throwing a NullPointerException. Automatically triggers internal capacity expansion if length() + str.length() exceeds capacity(). Returns the exact same StringBuilder reference ('this') for fluent chaining.
notes: Never concatenate with '+' inside loops; call sb.append() instead to prevent quadratic O(N^2) heap allocations.

name: append

arguments.name: i
arguments.description: The primitive integer value to convert and append

use: Appends the string representation of the primitive int argument directly to the internal character buffer without allocating an intermediate java.lang.String or Integer wrapper object on the heap.
notes: Internally delegates to Integer.getChars(int, int, byte[]) in modern JDKs for zero-allocation integer formatting.

name: append

arguments.name: d
arguments.description: The 64-bit IEEE 754 floating-point value to append

use: Appends the string representation of the double argument to this sequence via Double.toString(d). Handles special values such as NaN, POSITIVE_INFINITY, and NEGATIVE_INFINITY cleanly.
notes: For strict financial decimal rounding and formatting, prefer String.format("%.2f", price) or BigDecimal.

name: append

arguments.name: c
arguments.description: The 16-bit UTF-16 character literal to append

use: Appends a single char directly into the internal buffer array at index length(), incrementing length by 1. This is the fastest appending method in the entire Java SDK because it requires zero string parsing or object conversion.
notes: In high-throughput loops (e.g. CSV line generators), append(';') is significantly faster than append(";").

name: append
use: Appends the string representation of the boolean argument ("true" or "false") directly into the buffer without allocating an intermediate object.
notes: Writes the raw characters 't','r','u','e' directly into the backing buffer.

name: append
use: Appends the string representation of the Object argument by invoking String.valueOf(obj). If obj is null, the four characters "null" are safely appended without raising a NullPointerException. Otherwise, obj.toString() is called.
notes: Ensure custom objects have an efficient toString() implementation to avoid memory overhead when appending.

name: append
signature: public StringBuilder append(char[] str, int offset, int len)

arguments.name: offset
arguments.description: Starting index within the source array

use: Appends a sub-slice of a character array directly into the buffer using fast system array copying. Avoids the need to create a temporary String(str, offset, len) object, saving GC pressure in parsers and socket streams.
notes: Throws IndexOutOfBoundsException if offset < 0, len < 0, or offset + len > str.length.

name: append
signature: public StringBuilder append(CharSequence s, int start, int end)
use: Appends a subsequence of the specified CharSequence. If s is null, this method appends characters from the string "null" as if s were "null". Extremely useful when slicing data from an existing StringBuilder into another.
notes: The range is half-open: index start is included, but end is excluded.

name: appendCodePoint
use: Appends the string representation of the codePoint argument to this sequence. If the code point is within the supplementary character plane (> 0xFFFF), it automatically generates and appends both surrogate pair characters.
notes: Essential for internationalization (i18n) and modern emoji handling without corrupting multi-byte code units.

name: insert
signature: public StringBuilder insert(int offset, String str)

arguments.name: offset
arguments.description: The zero-based position at which to insert

use: Inserts the specified String into this character sequence at the specified index offset. Existing characters from offset onwards are shifted to the right. If str is null, "null" is inserted. If offset == length(), behavior is equivalent to append(str).
notes: Throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException if offset < 0 or offset > length().

name: insert
signature: public StringBuilder insert(int offset, int i)

arguments.name: i
arguments.description: The primitive int to convert and insert

use: Inserts the string representation of the primitive int into this sequence at the specified offset. Shifts following characters rightward.
notes: Does not allocate intermediate String wrappers.

name: insert
signature: public StringBuilder insert(int offset, char c)

arguments.name: offset
arguments.description: The index where the character will be inserted

use: Inserts the char argument into this sequence at the specified index. All characters originally at or after index are shifted one slot to the right.
notes: Useful for inserting delimiter brackets, commas, or quotes inside constructed sequences.

name: insert
signature: public StringBuilder insert(int offset, boolean b)
use: Inserts the string representation of boolean b ("true" or "false") into this character sequence at the position indicated by offset.
notes: Shifts trailing characters rightward by 4 (for true) or 5 (for false).

name: insert
signature: public StringBuilder insert(int offset, Object obj)

arguments.name: offset
arguments.description: The index at which to insert

arguments.name: obj
arguments.description: Object whose toString() will be inserted

use: Inserts the string representation of the Object argument into this character sequence at offset via String.valueOf(obj).
notes: If obj is null, the literal "null" is inserted safely.

name: insert
signature: public StringBuilder insert(int index, char[] str, int offset, int len)

arguments.name: index
arguments.description: Position in StringBuilder where insertion occurs

use: Inserts a sub-array of characters from str into this sequence at the specified index position. High performance bulk copy.
notes: Throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException if index < 0 or index > length().

name: replace
signature: public StringBuilder replace(int start, int end, String str)

arguments.name: str
arguments.description: String that will replace the previous contents

use: Replaces the characters in a substring of this sequence with characters in the specified String. The substring begins at start and extends to the character at index end - 1. If end > length(), end is capped to length(). The length of str does not need to match end - start.
notes: Returns 'this' allowing method chaining. If start > end or start < 0, throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.

name: setCharAt
signature: public void setCharAt(int index, char ch)

arguments.name: index
arguments.description: Index of the character to modify

use: Directly mutates the character at the specified index to ch in-place in O(1) time without shifting any surrounding characters. Note that this method returns void, which means it CANNOT be chained fluently.
notes: Throws IndexOutOfBoundsException if index < 0 or index >= length().

name: delete
signature: public StringBuilder delete(int start, int end)
use: Removes the characters in a substring of this sequence from start up to end - 1. The remaining characters are shifted left by end - start slots, and length() is decremented accordingly. If start == end, no changes occur. If end > length(), characters through the end of the buffer are deleted.
notes: Throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException if start < 0, start > length(), or start > end.

name: deleteCharAt

arguments.name: index
arguments.description: Index of the single character to be removed

use: Removes the character at the specified index position from this sequence. Shifts all subsequent characters one position to the left and decrements length() by 1.
notes: Throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException if index < 0 or index >= length().

name: reverse
use: Causes this character sequence to be replaced by the reverse of the sequence directly in place. If there are any surrogate pairs included in the sequence, these are treated as single characters for the reverse operation so emoji and unicode scripts do not get corrupted.
notes: Operates in O(N/2) swaps with zero heap allocations, making it ideal for palindrome verification algorithms.

name: repeat
signature: public StringBuilder repeat(CharSequence s, int count)

arguments.name: count
arguments.description: Number of times to append s (must be >= 0)

use: Appends count copies of the specified CharSequence s directly into this builder. Added in Java 21 to eliminate boilerplate for-loops when constructing separators, padding, or indentation lines.
notes: Throws IllegalArgumentException if count < 0. If count == 0, the builder is unchanged.

name: repeat
signature: public StringBuilder repeat(int codePoint, int count)
use: Appends count copies of the specified Unicode code point to this builder sequence. Native support for surrogate pairs.
notes: Optimized in JDK 21 for single byte fill operations when characters fit Latin-1.

name: capacity
use: Returns the current capacity of the StringBuilder. Capacity is the total amount of character storage currently allocated in the internal backing buffer, whereas length() is the number of characters currently occupied.
notes: Default capacity of empty constructor new StringBuilder() is always 16 characters.

name: length
use: Returns the number of characters currently stored in this sequence (the logical length). Implemented from CharSequence.
notes: length() is always <= capacity().

name: ensureCapacity
use: Ensures that the internal buffer capacity is at least equal to minimumCapacity. If current capacity is smaller, a larger internal array is allocated using the growth formula: max(minimumCapacity, (oldCapacity * 2) + 2).
notes: Use ensureCapacity() before a massive append loop to completely prevent repetitive array reallocation and copying overhead.

name: trimToSize
use: Attempts to reduce the storage used for the character sequence by reallocating the internal array to match exactly length(). If the buffer is already trimmed, no reallocation takes place.
notes: Useful when a large temporary buffer has finished building its payload and must stay in memory without wasting unused capacity.

name: setLength

arguments.name: newLength
arguments.description: The new length of this character sequence

use: Sets the length of this character sequence. If newLength is smaller than current length(), the sequence is truncated. If newLength is larger, null characters ('\0') are appended. Calling sb.setLength(0) instantly resets the builder for reuse without releasing the underlying capacity!
exampleOutput:
Original: CacheDataToReuse | cap: 32
Cleared length: 0 | cap: 32
Reused: Fresh
notes: sb.setLength(0) is a high-performance optimization pattern to reuse a single StringBuilder across thousands of loop cycles.

name: charAt
use: Returns the char value in this sequence at the specified index in O(1) time.
exampleOutput:
Char at 0: R
Char at 5: t
notes: Throws IndexOutOfBoundsException if index < 0 or index >= length().

name: indexOf
use: Returns the index within this sequence of the first occurrence of the specified substring, or -1 if the substring does not occur.
notes: Linear search over the internal character buffer.

name: indexOf
signature: public int indexOf(String str, int fromIndex)

arguments.name: fromIndex
arguments.description: The index from which to start the search

use: Returns the index within this sequence of the first occurrence of the specified substring, starting the search forward from fromIndex.
example:
StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("Learn Java, Love Java");
System.out.println("Second Java at: " + sb.indexOf("Java", 7));
notes: If fromIndex < 0, search starts at 0. If fromIndex >= length(), returns -1.

name: lastIndexOf
use: Returns the index within this sequence of the rightmost occurrence of the specified substring, searching backwards from the end.
example:
StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("server.prod.backup.log");
System.out.println("Last dot at: " + sb.lastIndexOf("."));
notes: Returns -1 if the substring is not found.

name: lastIndexOf
signature: public int lastIndexOf(String str, int fromIndex)

arguments.name: fromIndex
arguments.description: The index to start searching backwards from

use: Returns the index within this sequence of the last occurrence of the specified substring, searching backwards starting at fromIndex.
example:
StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("alpha/beta/gamma/delta");
System.out.println("Slash before index 12: " + sb.lastIndexOf("/", 12));
notes: Useful in token parsing and reverse string segmentations.

name: substring
use: Returns a new immutable java.lang.String that contains a subsequence of characters currently contained in this character sequence starting from start up to length(). Notice that this returns a String, NOT a StringBuilder!
exampleOutput:
Extracted code: 9021
Original sb unchanged: Order-9021
notes: Does not mutate the invoking StringBuilder. Allocates a new String on the heap.

name: substring
signature: public String substring(int start, int end)
use: Returns a new immutable java.lang.String containing the substring from index start to end - 1.
notes: Throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException if start < 0, start > end, or end > length().

name: subSequence
signature: public CharSequence subSequence(int start, int end)
use: Returns a new CharSequence that is a subsequence of this sequence. Implements CharSequence.subSequence(). Simply calls this.substring(start, end) under the hood.
notes: Provided for generic CharSequence polymorphism.

name: getChars
signature: public void getChars(int srcBegin, int srcEnd, char[] dst, int dstBegin)

arguments.name: dstBegin
arguments.description: Offset in dst array where writing begins

use: Fast bulk memory copy of characters from this sequence into a destination char[] array. Zero intermediate heap object creation.
notes: Optimal for high-throughput networking codecs and protocol serializations.

name: toString
use: Returns a standard immutable java.lang.String representing the character sequence currently stored in this StringBuilder. Modern JVMs (Java 9+) use Compact Strings byte arrays and may share storage safely using copy-on-write semantics.
exampleOutput:
String value: Final Output
Is String? true
notes: Calling sb.toString() is the final step in any mutable buffer assembly pipeline.

name: compareTo
use: Compares two StringBuilder instances lexicographically in Java 11+. Returns 0 if both sequences contain identical characters in the same order, a negative integer if this sequence precedes another, or a positive integer if this sequence follows another.
exampleOutput:
a vs b: -1
a vs c: 0
notes: Added in Java 11 because StringBuilder now implements Comparable<StringBuilder>!

name: append
use: Appends the string to this thread-safe buffer. Uses the 'synchronized' keyword on the method declaration, which acquires the intrinsic object monitor lock before writing to the internal buffer. Guarantees safety when multiple concurrent threads share the same StringBuffer instance.
notes: Synchronization introduces locking overhead. Use StringBuilder unless thread safety across shared instances is explicitly required.

name: insert
signature: public synchronized StringBuffer insert(int offset, String str)
use: Thread-safe synchronized insertion at index offset. Protects concurrent threads from data corruption and race conditions during buffer reallocation.
notes: Synchronized on 'this' monitor.

name: delete
signature: public synchronized StringBuffer delete(int start, int end)
use: Thread-safe synchronized deletion of character range [start, end). Acquires the monitor lock before shifting characters left.
notes: Guarantees atomic range removal.

name: reverse
use: Thread-safe in-place reversal of the character sequence. Ensures that concurrent readers or writers cannot observe an intermediate corrupted state during the swap operations.
notes: Synchronized method.

name: toString
use: Synchronized snapshot generation. Creates a new immutable String while holding the monitor lock to ensure the returned String reflects a coherent state.
notes: Historical design; in modern code prefer java.util.concurrent abstractions.

name: printf
signature: public PrintStream printf(String format, Object... args)

arguments.name: format
arguments.description: Format string with conversion specifiers and flags

arguments.name: args
arguments.description: Varargs arguments referenced by format specifiers

use: A convenience method to write a formatted string to this output stream using the specified format string and varargs. Internally equivalent to out.format(format, args). Returns the PrintStream for convenient chaining.
notes:
Always use %n instead of 
 for platform-independent newline generation (
 on Windows, 
 on Linux/macOS).

name: printf
signature: public PrintStream printf(Locale l, String format, Object... args)
use: Writes formatted output using an explicit Locale. Critical for internationalization where number grouping, currency signs, and decimal separators vary across countries (e.g. Germany uses ',' for decimal and '.' for thousands).
notes: Prevents regional server configuration bugs from breaking financial reports.

name: format
signature: public static String format(String format, Object... args)
use: Returns a formatted String using the default locale and specified format string and arguments. Does NOT print to console; instead creates and returns an immutable formatted String object on the heap.
notes: Specifier syntax: %[argument_index$][flags][width][.precision]conversion.

name: format
signature: public static String format(Locale l, String format, Object... args)
use: Returns a formatted String evaluated under the specified Locale rules.
example:
String invoice = String.format(java.util.Locale.ITALY, "Importo: %,.2f EUR", 9876.50);
System.out.println(invoice);
notes: Essential for generating multi-currency financial invoices.

name: formatted

arguments.name: args
arguments.description: Arguments referenced by the format specifiers

use: Formats using this string as the format string and the supplied arguments. Equivalent to String.format(this, args). Introduced in Java 15 as an instance method specifically to make formatting Java Text Blocks clean, fluid, and readable without nested static calls.
exampleOutput: SELECT * FROM users WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND age >= 18
notes: Preferred over String.format(...) when formatting multi-line Text Blocks.

name: format
signature: public Formatter format(String format, Object... args)
use: Directly appends formatted output into a target Appendable destination, such as a custom StringBuilder instance. Prevents intermediate string object allocation when accumulating formatted reports into a single builder.
notes: Always flush() or close() if Formatter wraps an external file or socket stream.

name: stripIndent
use: Returns a string whose value is this string, with incidental white space removed from the beginning and end of every line. Calculates the common minimum leading whitespace across all non-empty lines and strips it uniformly.
notes: Invoked automatically by the Java 15+ compiler during text block processing, but can also be invoked manually on dynamic strings.

name: translateEscapes
use: Returns a string whose value is this string, with escape sequences (such as \n, \t, \b, \r, \", \', and octal/unicode escapes) translated into their corresponding literal characters as if the string was compiled in source code.
notes: Very useful when reading templates from external configuration files or database tables and interpreting escapes at runtime.

name: indent

arguments.name: n
arguments.description: Number of spaces to add (positive) or strip (negative)

use: Adjusts the indentation of each line of this string based on n. If n > 0, n spaces are inserted at the beginning of each line. If n < 0, up to |n| leading whitespace characters are removed from each line. Each line is normalized to end with a \n newline.
notes: Introduced in Java 12; pairs cleanly with Text Blocks and code generation templates.
